content: Oseltamivir, marketed as TAMIFLU, is approved for the treatment of acute, uncomplicated illness caused by influenza infection in patients who are 2 weeks of age and older, provided they have been symptomatic for no more than 2 days. TAMIFLU is also indicated for the prevention (prophylaxis) of influenza in individuals aged 1 year and older. There are several important limitations to the use of TAMIFLU that should be considered before initiating treatment or prophylaxis: 1. The efficacy of TAMIFLU has not been established in patients who begin treatment more than 48 hours after the onset of symptoms. 2. TAMIFLU is not a replacement for annual influenza vaccination, which remains the primary method of influenza prevention as recommended by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices. 3. There is no evidence to support the efficacy of TAMIFLU in treating illnesses caused by pathogens other than influenza virus types A and B. 4. Influenza viruses are known to evolve over time. The emergence of resistance mutations may reduce the effectiveness of the drug. Additionally, other factors, such as changes in the virulence of the virus, may also diminish the clinical benefits of antiviral medications. 5. Prescribers should take into account the most current information on influenza drug susceptibility patterns and treatment outcomes when deciding whether to use TAMIFLU.
